findings.subject: Alaska AS 12.55.085 versus AS 12.55.078
findings.dispositionNote: E2-D proposed registry_scoped_out_named_authority on the same evidence. The stop condition here is an upstream intake-memo deferral rather than a registry stop condition naming the authority, which is the fact pattern the committed batch-1 authority crosswalk labels reconciled_deferred_blocker / missing_from_current_normalization. Final E3 picks the canonical label; the two proposals agree on every substantive fact and differ only in vocabulary.
findings.mechanism: Set-aside of a conviction after successful completion of a Suspended Imposition of Sentence, granted by the sentencing court under AS 12.55.085(e), with categorical exclusions at AS 12.55.085(f). The relief is a set-aside plus certificate; the conviction record is not sealed or expunged and remains usable as a sentencing prior.
findings.statuteDistinction: AS 12.55.078 (suspended entry of judgment) is a different mechanism, not an alternate citation for the same one: SEJ withholds entry of judgment and ends in dismissal without a conviction — which is why the ak-courtview track lists an AS 12.55.078 dismissal as a non-conviction ground — while an SIS under AS 12.55.085 produces a conviction the court may later set aside. Adjacent section numbers and the shared word 'suspended' are not evidence of equivalence, and the registry's ak-sej track is additionally restricted to in-case administration with no later participant filing.
findings.registryRelationship: No registry track carries AS 12.55.085 as operative authority. The omission is deliberate and documented upstream: the Alaska legal-design intake memo declares an eleventh AK track ak-set-aside, legal name 'Set-Aside After a Suspended Imposition of Sentence, AS 12.55.085', authority 'AS 12.55.085, with the set-aside at (e) and the exclusions at (f)', held at legalDesignDecision.status legal_research_required because whether a person discharged years ago without a set-aside can still obtain one, and by what vehicle, is unresolved.
findings.runtimeEffect: The compiled pathway stays live but contributes no per-track coverage until the registry owner registers ak-set-aside or records a terminal disposition.
findings.denominatorEffect: None from this lane. Registering ak-set-aside would raise the denominator 497 -> 498; that decision belongs to the registry owner with counsel resolving the open legal question in the intake memo.
findings.currentness: No supersession issue identified in committed sources.
findings.approvalOwner: Registry owner with counsel (the intake memo's legal_research_required question is a counsel question).

findings.subject: Louisiana trafficking fee-exempt route operative relief authority

proposedMapping.architectureDeclaration: The Louisiana state pack declares the trafficking-victim route as one certification overlay spanning the arts. 977 and 978 motions, which is the committed architecture the canonical crosswalk requires before a one-pathway-to-two-tracks relationship may land.

findings.mechanism: The relief mechanism is the standard conviction-expungement motions themselves — La. C.Cr.P. art. 977 (misdemeanor) and art. 978 (felony). The trafficking element is a district-attorney certification that the offense was committed substantially because of trafficking victimization; when obtained it waives the arts. 977/978 time delays and exempts the applicant from expungement fees. It creates no separate relief vehicle.

operativeAuthority.subsection: trafficking-certification paragraphs; exact paragraph letters not pinned in any committed source

findings.authorityClassification: Relief authority: arts. 977/978 (the motions). Eligibility/timing overlay: the DA trafficking certification waiving the delays. Fee authority: the fee-exemption effect (art. 983 family in the compiled profile's fee discussion) — expressly NOT relief authority, and this record does not treat it as such. The compiled pathway's own rule clauses carry only the fee/intake material, which is why automatic matching correctly refused to map it; the relief identity comes from the state pack.

findings.subject: Mississippi DUI nonadjudication operative citation
findings.mechanism: The once-only DUI nonadjudication program inside Miss. Code Ann. § 63-11-30: the court withholds adjudication and sentencing and places the person in a nonadjudication program; eligibility is once per lifetime under any nonadjudication law, all court-imposed terms must be completed, and a CDL or commercial learner's permit at the time of the offense disqualifies.

operativeAuthority.subsection: nonadjudication subsection — expected (14); not pinned in any committed source

findings.registryRelationship: The registry consolidates § 63-11-30 relief in the ms-dui track and does so knowingly: its own routing statement bars implied-consent expunction in intervention court and sends those matters to the § 63-11-30 DUI track, and the ms-dui record itself treats a prior DUI nonadjudication as a disqualifying event — the registry situates the nonadjudication program inside this track's subject matter. ms-nonadj is statutorily distinct (§ 99-15-26).
findings.runtimeEffect: Contributes runtime coverage as a variant of ms-dui once final E3 lands the mapping.

findings.subject: Pennsylvania Rule 490/790 venue or composition discriminator

proposedMapping.architectureDeclaration: The registry itself declares the fork rule inside pa_490_nonconviction: Rule 490 governs expungement in summary cases; any case in which a summary offense was filed together with a misdemeanor, felony or murder charge proceeds under Rule 790 instead — with a matching stop condition and a venue predicate (whether the case remained at the magisterial district court). The two tracks share operative 18 Pa.C.S. § 9122(a) and identical non-conviction disposition classes.

findings.mechanism: Petition for expungement of non-conviction records under 18 Pa.C.S. § 9122(a). The registry implements it as one mechanism with a declared procedural fork: pure summary cases before a magisterial district judge proceed under Pa.R.Crim.P. 490; court cases, including any case carrying a misdemeanor, felony or murder charge, proceed under Pa.R.Crim.P. 790.
findings.discriminator: Case composition and venue, registry-declared: summary-only case that remained at the magisterial district court -> Rule 490; otherwise -> Rule 790. The discriminator is committed; what is missing is not evidence but a compiled-profile input — path-a carries no question capturing case composition or venue.
findings.proposedProfileCorrection: Add one screening input to the PA profile for path-a: whether the case was a summary-offense case handled at the magisterial district court (and whether any misdemeanor, felony or murder charge was filed in the same case). Owned by the profile/implementation lane; not made by this lane.
findings.runtimeEffect: Contributes runtime coverage across the declared pair once final E3 lands the mapping; until the profile correction lands, packet assembly cannot select between the Rule 490 and Rule 790 form sets and the pathway should be treated as covered-with-metadata-gap.
findings.currentness: The registry's pa_acquittal_auto notes automatic acquittal expungement; no supersession issue affects the 490/790 fork itself in committed sources.
findings.approvalOwner: Final E3 for the pair mapping; the compiled-profile owner for the venue/composition question.
